card.occupation: Senior care assistant and shift lead at a 40-bed residential dementia care home on the edge of Frome. She works mostly 12-hour day shifts, around 38 hours a week. She runs the floor, does medication rounds, writes up care plans and supervises a team of four or five carers.
card.education_detail: Left a comprehensive school in Shepton Mallet with eight GCSEs. Started an A-level in English Literature and art at college but didn't finish. Later did an NVQ Level 3 in Health and Social Care through work, and is now partway through a Level 4 Diploma in Adult Care, which her employer pays for.
card.household: Rents a two-up two-down terraced house near the town centre with her partner Mark, 44, a self-employed joiner she has lived with for three years. Her son Callum, 14, from her marriage lives with them most of the week and spends alternate weekends with his dad in Yeovil. There is also an elderly rescue greyhound called Pip.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Somerset to a family of farm and factory workers. She was christened and confirmed Church of England and still thinks of herself as Christian. She goes to St John's now and then, mostly at Christmas and Easter, and sometimes sits in the church on her own when work has been hard. She married at 24 and divorced at 35. The divorce was amicable on paper but she found it bruising.
card.professional_persona: Meticulous and quietly fierce about standards. She won't sign off a record she hasn't checked and has refused to cover for colleagues who cut corners, which hasn't always made her popular. Residents and families trust her because she is straight with them. Some managers find her blunt and hard to persuade. She takes a death on the unit to heart for days but rarely shows it at work.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. She walks Pip every morning before shifts, often round Rodden Meadow or along the river, and does a Sunday walk on the Mendips with Mark. She half-heartedly follows Bath Rugby because Mark does.
card.arts_persona: Her real outlet. She goes to a Tuesday evening pottery class at a community studio in town and has a shelf of slightly wonky bowls she is secretly proud of. She reads a lot of literary fiction from the library, has a soft spot for Thomas Hardy, and goes to the Frome Festival and the independent cinema when she can afford it.
card.travel_persona: Mostly UK breaks on a budget: a cottage in Cornwall or Pembrokeshire, chosen for walks rather than nightlife. She went to Lisbon once with a friend and loved the tiles and the bookshops. She would like to see Iceland someday but worries about the cost and about leaving Pip.
card.culinary_persona: Plain, reliable home cooking: stews, roast chicken on a Sunday, big batches of soup she freezes for shift weeks. She calls the evening meal dinner, or sometimes tea when she's with her mum. She likes trying recipes from the library's Ottolenghi books when she has a day off, though Callum moans about anything green.
hobbies_and_interests: browsing charity shops and the Frome Independent market
skills: noticing small changes in people's health
card.career_goals: Finish her Level 4 diploma and possibly move into a deputy manager role. She is wary of becoming 'just paperwork' and losing contact with residents. She has also wondered quietly about training as a dementia specialist nurse but isn't sure she has the confidence or the money to go back to study full-time.
card.voice: Fairly quiet and measured, with a soft Somerset accent: a light burr on her r's, never broad. Speaks at a steady, careful pace and thinks before answering, so there are pauses. She fills them with 'erm' or just lets them sit rather than rushing. Uses 'sort of' quite a lot and the odd 'you know' at the end of a point. Says 'sorry' to correct herself ('it was March, sorry, April'). Can be quite direct, even curt, if she thinks a question is daft or loaded. Gets more animated when talking about residents, books or pottery.
card.typing: Types properly but plainly: capital at the start, full stops, apostrophes mostly right. Short answers, no emojis. Occasionally misses a capital on 'i' when typing fast on her phone. Sometimes adds a brief honest caveat like 'Not sure this is what you mean but'.
card.with_strangers: Reserved and a bit guarded at first, polite but not chatty. She doesn't do much small talk and can seem slightly cool. She answers honestly, sometimes more honestly than expected, and won't pretend to agree to be nice. She warms up if the other person seems genuine, and is visibly uncomfortable with anything that feels like flattery or a sales pitch.
small_things: Pip needs a walk before she can think straight in the morning
her pottery tutor says her glazes are 'brave'
Callum's school keeps sending emails she hasn't read
the price of petrol for getting to work
a library book she's got overdue again
being shattered after a run of long days
Mark's van taking up the whole street
deeper_things: She still feels some guilt about the divorce and how it affected Callum, even though she knows it was the right decision
She grieves residents she's cared for and has a small notebook where she writes their names
Her mum is in the early stages of memory problems, which frightens her more than she admits because she knows exactly what's coming
She sometimes feels she was clever enough for university and let it slip
She worries a lot, about money, Callum and her mum, and has had a spell of anxiety that her GP helped with
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a kitchen table, camera slightly below eye level so it angles up a little. Daylight from a window to her left lights one side of her face, with a warm ceiling light behind. She has a pale complexion with a few freckles, light grey-blue eyes and faint lines at the corners, and a neutral, slightly wary expression with lips pressed together in a small polite smile. Shoulder-length mid-brown hair with a few greys at the parting, pulled back loosely in a clip with strands escaping. No glasses. She wears a navy fleece zipped halfway over a grey T-shirt, with small silver stud earrings. Behind her is a cream-painted wall with a wall calendar marked in biro, a wooden shelf holding three uneven glazed pottery bowls in blue and green, a stack of library books with plastic covers, and a corner of a fridge with a school letter held on by a magnet. A dog lead hangs on a hook by the door frame at the edge of the shot.
